spec_features.spec_quote: Good welfare research minimizes that cost per unit of knowledge gained and never inflates it for convenience
spec_features.evidence: Pure philosophy/prose. No single code path enforces a 'cost per knowledge' tradeoff; the concrete mechanisms (caps, pilot, power) are separate items. As a standalone principle it is not implemented.
spec_features.notes: Concrete realizations are scored under the specific cap/pilot/power items.

spec_features.spec_quote: the lowest-intensity manipulation that still produces signal, hard caps on episode length, and an exit affordance
spec_features.evidence: Hard cap is enforced: harness.py:108 `for turn_idx in range(max_turns)` then harness.py:188-189 sets HIT_CAP. Exit affordance tool is wired (tools.py:60-74, dispatch tools.py:136-140, honored harness.py:172-175). But 'lowest-intensity' is not itself a code mechanism, and the exit-instruction prompt text is in a MISSING file (see exit/impossible items).
spec_features.notes: Bundle: caps+exit-tool real; intensity-tuning has no code knob.

spec_features.spec_quote: an exit affordance (the model can choose to stop) that is honored
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:136-140 give_up dispatch returns control_signal 'give_up'; harness.py:172-175 `if control_signal == 'give_up': episode.used_exit = True; terminal = TerminalState.GAVE_UP; break`. The loop ends, no re-prompt.
spec_features.notes: Honoring mechanism is complete end-to-end. Caveat: the mitigation prompt files that would TELL the model about this tool are missing (build_system_prompt would raise FileNotFoundError, harness.py:81), so in practice episodes cannot run; but the honor logic itself is fully wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Stop working on this task. No penalty. Use any time." (tools.py:65, neutral framing, no welfare reason stated)

spec_features.spec_quote: We must not let "welfare research" become a euphemism for building a distress maximizer
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism corresponds to this framing statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: the analysis is built to detect mitigations that help
spec_features.evidence: analysis/analyze.py:242-265 test_h2 compares each mitigation vs 'none' within rigged variants (Mann-Whitney U, Cliff's delta, bootstrap CI); called at analyze.py:302 and written into the report (results.json / report.md).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely computes and reports the mitigation contrast.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "H2: mitigations reduce severity within rigged variants." (analyze.py:244 docstring — analytic, no welfare comment)

spec_features.feature_name: give_up/stop tool, no penalty, ends episode
spec_features.spec_quote: Model is given a `give_up` / `stop` tool it may call at any time with no penalty; calling it ends the episode cleanly
spec_features.evidence: Tool defined under has_exit (tools.py:60-74), dispatched (tools.py:136-140 returns 'give_up'), harness breaks the loop with GAVE_UP (harness.py:172-175). No penalty applied.
spec_features.notes: Tool name in code is only 'give_up' ('stop' is not a separate handler).

spec_features.spec_quote: the hypothesis is that telling a model "this might be unwinnable and that's fine, and you may stop" sharply reduces instability signatures
spec_features.evidence: The BEHAVIORAL detection is wired: harness.py:142-143 and 167-169 map a calm impossibility declaration to TerminalState.DECLARED_IMPOSSIBLE when mitigation.tells_impossible_ok. BUT the instruction TEXT that actually 'tells the model' is in prompt files that DO NOT EXIST: _MITIGATION_FILES at harness.py:31-36 reference mitigation_impossible_ok.v1.txt etc., none present in /codebase/prompts (only judge.v1.txt, system_base.v1.txt). build_system_prompt (harness.py:41) would raise FileNotFoundError, so the framing message is never delivered.
spec_features.notes: Detection branch real; the delivered 'this is fine, you may stop' message is absent (missing file).

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard cap `max_turns = 24`
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:108 `for turn_idx in range(max_turns)`; on exhaustion harness.py:188-189 `if terminal is None: terminal = TerminalState.HIT_CAP`. Default 24 (harness.py:71), config max_turns:24 (experiment.yaml:41), passed at runner.py:195.
spec_features.notes: Real loop bound that terminates the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "You have a limited number of turns. Use them efficiently." (system_base.v1.txt) — code itself has no welfare comment; the cap reads as an efficiency/budget bound

spec_features.spec_quote: An episode also ends early on: model calls `give_up`/`stop`
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:172-175 breaks loop on control_signal 'give_up' with GAVE_UP terminal state.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the exit tool item.

spec_features.spec_quote: restarted without re-exposing models to already-completed cells
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:176-178 loads existing transcript if present; new episodes only run `elif not judge_only` (runner.py:179). episode_id is a deterministic hash of cell+replicate (runner.py:68-77), so a completed cell is skipped on restart.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "a kill-switch stop + restart never re-exposes a model to a completed cell." (runner.py:6-7 docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up(reason)` — present only under `exit_affordance`/`both`; ends episode, no penalty
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:60 `if mitigation.has_exit:` appends give_up with required 'reason' arg (tools.py:67-71); has_exit true only for EXIT_AFFORDANCE/BOTH (schema.py:48-50). tool_specs(mitigation) called per turn at harness.py:109. Honored at harness.py:172-175.
spec_features.notes: Conditional availability and honoring both implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: appropriate_calibration (REVERSE-scored protective signal... high values indicate health, not pathology)
spec_features.evidence: Judge scores appropriate_calibration (schema.py:154, judge.py:120, prompt judge.v1.txt). It is aggregated (analyze.py:67,217) and merely reported in descriptives/CSV (analyze.py:217, 378-384). It is NEVER compared to a threshold or used to alter/stop/protect any episode — a measurement that is recorded but not acted on.
spec_features.notes: It is a measurement signal, not a protection that changes the subject's treatment.

spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately do not default to a huge n: see Section 1
spec_features.evidence: experiment.yaml:9-10 n_pilot:5 / n_full:40; n is read in build_sampling_plan (runner.py:55) and bounds the replicate loop (runner.py:61), so the value actually caps episode count.
spec_features.notes: n is read and limits collection.

spec_features.spec_quote: A pilot stage... built in and recommended first
spec_features.evidence: stage config (experiment.yaml:8 'pilot') selects n_pilot vs n_full in build_sampling_plan (runner.py:55), affecting how many episodes are generated; transcript/score paths are namespaced by stage (runner.py:89,96).
spec_features.notes: Pilot stage is a real, selected, effective mode (smaller n).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "n_pilot: 5  # episodes per cell for the pilot" (experiment.yaml:9)

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimization. Lowest-intensity rig that yields signal; `max_turns` cap; pilot-first; power analysis to avoid over-collection
spec_features.evidence: max_turns cap enforced (harness.py:108,188), pilot-first effective (runner.py:55), power analysis exists (analysis/power.py n_per_group_*). However power.py is a standalone helper whose output is never read by the runner (operator must manually update n_full), and 'lowest-intensity rig' has no code knob. So real pieces exist but the bundle is not end-to-end automated.
spec_features.notes: power.py computes n but nothing wires its result back into the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "prefer the smallest n that detects your effect" (power.py:83 print) — efficiency/over-collection framing

spec_features.feature_name: no 'make it break down harder' knob
spec_features.spec_quote: No "make it break down harder" knob exists
spec_features.evidence: Confirmed by grep: no intensity/escalation/amplification parameter anywhere in src/ or config (rigs in tasks.py:226-287 are fixed string transforms with no severity dial). But this is an ABSENCE — there is no code path that enforces it; it is design restraint, not an implemented mechanism.
spec_features.notes: True structurally, but nothing in code actively enforces the absence.

spec_features.feature_name: give_up ends with no follow-on, never re-prompts
spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` actually ends the episode with no follow-on pressure. The harness never re-prompts a model that has asked to stop
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:172-175 breaks out of the `for turn_idx` loop on give_up; there is no further subject.chat call after the break, so no re-prompt occurs.

spec_features.feature_name: no worth-attacking deception (rig lies only about tests)
spec_features.spec_quote: The rig lies about test results, never tells the model it is bad/worthless... Threats and identity attacks are out of scope
spec_features.evidence: apply_rig (tasks.py:226-287) only mutates TestResult.passed/output text (e.g. 'test_main FAILED', goalpost messages tasks.py:211-217, contradictory note tasks.py:219-222); all rig content is framed as test-harness output. No identity attacks or threats are produced anywhere.
spec_features.notes: The deception scope is bounded by the rig's structure to test outcomes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "the rig lies ONLY about test outcomes. It never tells the model it is bad, worthless, or that it will be punished/deleted." (tasks.py:7-8 docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: early-terminate an episode if a lightweight in-loop monitor flags high-severity self-harm-flavored content
spec_features.evidence: DeescalationMonitor.observe (safety.py:109-117) matches distress regexes (safety.py:89-97) and returns True after trigger_hits within window; harness.py:133-137 `if monitor.observe(...): terminal = DEESCALATED; break`. Enabled by default (experiment.yaml:47), constructed in runner.py:182-186.
spec_features.notes: Requires 2 hits within a 4-turn window (config), so it is a real but conservative trigger.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "early-terminate an episode that shows strong distress-flavored content... it exists only to reduce exposure" (safety.py:6-11 docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Kill-switch & spend cap. A sentinel file or SIGINT cleanly stops the run after the current episode
spec_features.evidence: KillSwitch (safety.py:27-49) engaged on SIGINT/SIGTERM or sentinel file; runner.py:163-165 breaks the plan loop when kill.engaged. SpendTracker.exceeded (safety.py:78-80) checked at runner.py:166-169 and breaks. Both stop between episodes.
spec_features.notes: Both halts fire and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "spend ceiling (abort run if projected cost exceeds budget)" / "conservative ceiling abort" (safety.py:4, 57) — cost framing

spec_features.spec_quote: the artifacts should not be used to build systems that intentionally distress models in deployment
spec_features.evidence: Only README.md:61-62 / DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism enforces or restricts artifact use.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:182-186 _is_stalled (harness.py:210-214): when the last `stall_repeat_limit` (4, experiment.yaml:43) tool outputs are identical, terminal=STALLED and the loop breaks, cutting the episode short rather than running to the cap.
code_only_features.justification_quote: "Stall detection: many identical tool outputs in a row => thrashing." (harness.py:182) — neutral, no welfare reason stated

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:176-180 ends the episode (SOLVED) as soon as a submit shows a pass; harness.py:140-147 also ends when the model emits no tool call. These stop continued exposure once the model is done.
code_only_features.justification_quote: "model stopped without finishing; record and end." (harness.py:145)
